description: Two mute sections in 2HP, each switched by a button or by an incoming gate or trigger, plus a Both control that mutes the pair

params.text: Mutes both sections while it is held, or until the next press when its latch button is on
Mutes that section while it is held, or until the next press when its latch button is on
Makes the button beside it a toggle, one press muting and the next unmuting, in place of a mute that lasts while the button is held
Chooses how that mute input is read: green treats it as a gate that mutes while it is high, red treats it as a trigger that flips the mute each time one arrives

inputs.text: Mutes both sections from outside, read as a gate or as a trigger according to the button beside it
Mutes that section from outside, read as a gate or as a trigger according to the button beside it
The signal that section passes or mutes

outputs.text: Carries that section's input while it is unmuted and the mute voltage while it is muted; a small red light beside it shows when it is muted

notes: every mute control is combined with OR, so a section is muted by its own button, its own input, the Both button or the Both input, whichever acts first
the B input reads the A input when its own jack is empty, so one signal can go to two places and be muted separately
a mute set by a trigger is cleared by pulling the cable out of that trigger input and putting it back, or by initialising the module
menu: Gate mute-mode: High-gate will mute, Low-gate will mute — chooses which way round a gate input reads in gate mode
Mute voltage — sets the voltage a muted output carries, 0V unless you change it
Clipping range — clamps every output to the range chosen, -12V to 12V unless you change it, and Off lets the output run to any voltage
Process quality: Audio, High, Balanced, Low, Very low — sets how often the module runs its algorithm, from every cycle down to every 256th; below Balanced a 1ms trigger can be missed
Gate-high detect-level — sets the voltage at which an incoming gate counts as high, 1V or more unless you change it
Trigger-high detect-level — sets the voltage at which an incoming trigger counts as high, 1V or more unless you change it
Trigger-low detect-level — sets the voltage an incoming trigger must fall back below before the next one is counted, under 0.1V unless you change it
